dataEntries.name: Multiple Deprivation Measure decile (NIMDM 2017, by Small Area)
dataEntries.description: Northern Ireland Multiple Deprivation Measure 2017 (NIMDM17) overall rank grouped into deciles at 2011 Small Area level: decile 1 = the 10% most deprived Small Areas, decile 10 = the 10% least deprived (of 4,537). Shaded on a viridis ramp; the table panel shows the underlying MDM rank plus the Income and Employment domain ranks. The deciles are Civgraph's, cutting NISRA's ranks into ten equal-sized groups. Ranks and deciles are relative: they place each area against the other areas of Northern Ireland in this edition only, so they say which areas are more deprived than others, not how deprived an area is in absolute terms. They cannot be compared across years (NIMDM 2017, 2010 and 2005 use different indicators, data years and methods) or with the Pobal HP Deprivation Index in the Republic, which is built differently; an area that moves between editions has not necessarily become more or less deprived. dataEntries.name: Multiple Deprivation Measure (NIMDM 2017, by Super Output Area)
dataEntries.description: The Northern Ireland Multiple Deprivation Measure 2017 (NIMDM 2017), published by NISRA on 23 November 2017, for the 890 Super Output Areas. Each area is shaded by its overall Multiple Deprivation Measure decile. Clicking an area shows its overall rank and decile, its rank and decile on each of the seven domains (Income; Employment; Health Deprivation and Disability; Education, Skills and Training; Access to Services; Living Environment; Crime and Disorder), the Housing Quality, Housing Access and Outdoor Physical Environment sub-domain ranks, the Crime and Disorder sub-domain ranks, the income- and employment-deprived shares of the population, and the income deprivation affecting children and older people. Most indicators relate to 2015/16. Rank 1 is the most deprived area and decile 1 the most deprived tenth of areas; decile 10 is the least deprived tenth. On the map decile 1 is darkest (dark purple) and decile 10 lightest (yellow). The deciles are Civgraph's, cutting NISRA's ranks into ten equal-sized groups. Ranks and deciles are relative: they place each area against the other areas of Northern Ireland in this edition only, so they say which areas are more deprived than others, not how deprived an area is in absolute terms. They cannot be compared across years (NIMDM 2017, 2010 and 2005 use different indicators, data years and methods) or with the Pobal HP Deprivation Index in the Republic, which is built differently; an area that moves between editions has not necessarily become more or less deprived. The figures are drawn on Civgraph's Super Output Area map (soa-2011): NISRA's 890 Super Output Areas, built from the 2001 Census Output Areas and used until Census 2021; every area matched. Source: NISRA, Northern Ireland Multiple Deprivation Measure 2017 (NIMDM2017), SOA level results (https://www.nisra.gov.uk/publications/nimdm17-soa-level-results), Crown copyright, reused under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

source.title: NISRA, Northern Ireland Multiple Deprivation Measure 2017 (NIMDM2017), SOA level results

dataEntries.name: Multiple Deprivation Measure (NIMDM 2010, by Output Area)
dataEntries.description: The Northern Ireland Multiple Deprivation Measure 2010 (NIMDM 2010), published by NISRA in 2010, for the 5,022 Output Areas of the 2001 Census. Each area is shaded by its overall Multiple Deprivation Measure decile. Clicking an area shows its overall score, rank and decile and the four domains NISRA published at Output Area level (Income; Employment; Proximity to Services; Crime and Disorder). Most indicators relate to 2007-2009. Rank 1 is the most deprived area and decile 1 the most deprived tenth of areas; decile 10 is the least deprived tenth. On the map decile 1 is darkest (dark purple) and decile 10 lightest (yellow). The deciles are Civgraph's, cutting NISRA's ranks into ten equal-sized groups. Where scores are given, a higher score is more deprived; scores on different domains are on different scales. Ranks and deciles are relative: they place each area against the other areas of Northern Ireland in this edition only, so they say which areas are more deprived than others, not how deprived an area is in absolute terms. They cannot be compared across years (NIMDM 2017, 2010 and 2005 use different indicators, data years and methods) or with the Pobal HP Deprivation Index in the Republic, which is built differently; an area that moves between editions has not necessarily become more or less deprived. The figures are drawn on Civgraph's Output Area map (oa-2001): the 5,022 Output Areas of the 2001 Census; every area matched. Source: NISRA, Northern Ireland Multiple Deprivation Measure 2010 (NIMDM2010), OA results (https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/deprivation-and-poverty/northern-ireland-multiple-deprivation-measure-2010-nimdm2010), Crown copyright, reused under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

dataEntries.name: Pobal HP Deprivation Index (2016, by Electoral Division)
dataEntries.description: The Pobal HP Deprivation Index for 2016, by Trutz Haase and Jonathan Pratschke for Pobal, calculated from Census 2016, for the Electoral Divisions of the Republic of Ireland. Each ED is shaded by its relative index category. The relative score is scaled so that 0 is the national average: a lower (more negative) score is more disadvantaged and a higher score more affluent. The categories are Pobal's 10-point bands, from 1 'extremely disadvantaged' (below -30, darkest) through 'marginally below average' (-10 to 0) and 'marginally above average' (0 to 10) to 8 'extremely affluent' (30 and above, lightest). Clicking an ED shows the score, Pobal's label, the population and the census indicators behind the index (population change, age dependency, lone parents, primary-only and third-level education, and male and female unemployment). The relative score compares each ED with the rest of the State in 2016 only, so it says which areas are more or less deprived than others, not how deprived an area is in absolute terms. It cannot be compared across years, and it cannot be compared with the Northern Ireland Multiple Deprivation Measure, which ranks areas on different indicators (there, rank 1 is the most deprived). The figures are drawn on Civgraph's Census 2011 Electoral Division map (eds-census-2011; 3,409 EDs), the nearest edition Civgraph holds: Pobal's 2016 units match it one to one, matched to Pobal's own ED map by area. Every one of the 3,409 mapped units has a value; 3,400 overlap their Pobal unit by 90% or more, and the rest, a few city EDs, by at least 80%, the difference being the two maps' generalisation. Source: Pobal HP Deprivation Index, Electoral Division 2016 (Pobal, https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=bb6b0b6a6e5a402893a37f340169426a), licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0).
